title: Apple GPU prefill BK16 shared staging versus direct control
question: With BM=8, BN=16, 128 threads, and one thread per output held fixed, does BK=16 shared operand staging beat direct full-K streaming on rotating packed-QKV prefill?
hypothesis: BK16's source-level operand reuse may repay its shared reads, writes, loop structure, 768-byte scratch allocation, and 112 barriers as M grows.

control.ownership: One 128-thread group owns one 8x16 output rectangle; one thread owns one scalar output and one persistent FP32 accumulator.
control.k_mapping: Each valid thread walks all K=896 values serially and loads X and W directly from device memory.

candidate.ownership: The same 128-thread group owns the same 8x16 output rectangle; one thread owns one scalar output and one persistent FP32 accumulator.
candidate.cooperative_load: Each phase stages an 8x16 X tile and a 16x16 W tile with zero fill at M, N, and K tails.

changed_mechanism: The candidate replaces repeated per-output device loads with cooperative shared operand staging and reuse. This necessarily also changes shared accesses, phase loops, bounds work, barriers, and generated code.
unchanged: BF16 input, weight, bias, and output with FP32 accumulation and one final BF16 cast
row-major X[M,K], W[N,K], and Y[M,N] layouts
128 threads and 128 output owners per complete output tile
one enqueue per layer and one completion boundary per measured workload
K=896, N=1152, and 24 distinct rotating weight allocations
no weight packing, quantization, or public dispatch change

correctness.authority: tests/test_linear.mojo plus each benchmark implementation's untimed exact-unit-output gate
required_cases: Existing direct-control oracle, exact-tile, ragged-tail, and Qwen-width cases
BK16 host-reference comparison at M=9 K=129 N=17
Exact BF16 unit output at K=896 and N=1152 before timing every benchmark specialization
Existing rowwise, BK32, BK64, BK128, decode, and packed-QKV tests remain passing

workload_matrix.weights: 24 distinct allocations rotated once per measured workload iteration

measurement_protocol.paired_statistic: Within each block and M, BK16 median divided by direct median; summarize the four ratios with their median and retain every ratio.
measurement_protocol.environment: Clean immutable commit, AC power, no reported thermal or performance warning, Apple GPU plus Metal runtime identity, and MODULAR_DEBUG unset.

classification_rule.material_improvement: Median paired ratio <= 0.95 and BK16 faster in at least three of four blocks.
classification_rule.material_regression: Median paired ratio >= 1.05 and BK16 slower in at least three of four blocks.

decision_rule.advance: Advance BK16 to a final public-rowwise comparison only if it materially improves M=64, 128, and 256 and does not materially regress any tested M>=8.
decision_rule.reject: If BK16 materially regresses M=64, 128, and 256, reject shared staging as an optimization for this scalar one-output-per-thread mapping and stop BK tuning.
decision_rule.otherwise: Make no advance or production change; retain the result as mixed or inconclusive before designing another experiment.
decision_rule.production_decision: None. Even an advancing result cannot select a public dispatch path.

nonclaims: The comparison isolates the complete shared-staging mechanism, not an individual barrier, cache, occupancy, shared-memory, instruction, or compiler effect.
Requested traffic is source-derived and is not observed hardware cache, fabric, or DRAM traffic.
A BK16 win against direct would not establish a win against the public SIMD-group rowwise kernel.
A BK16 loss would be specific to this scalar 8x16 arithmetic ownership and would not reject multi-output or hardware-matrix tiled mappings.
No end-to-end prompt, model, or decoder throughput result.
